facts.text: Léon's French roots, simple and exact
facts.why: Wikipedia has Léon as an Italian-American hitman who grew up in Italy, so French roots are wrong.
facts.fix: a sandwich as plain as Léon's habits

facts.text: the French touch, for a man of very simple habits
facts.why: Léon is an Italian immigrant in New York, and no source ties him to French food. The jambon-beurre note should only lean on his plain habits.
facts.fix: a plain sandwich for a man of very simple habits

facts.text: Léon drinks milk, two litres at a time
facts.why: Léon drinks milk throughout, but the line quoted for him is two quarts a day, not two litres at a time.
facts.fix: Léon drinks milk, two quarts a day

vibe.verdict: A moody Little Italy restaurant with the milk and the plant, but it skips Mathilda and Stansfield, who carry the film.
missing: 'Is life always this hard, or is it just when you're a kid?' (Mathilda)
'Give it roots' (the plant in the school field)
Mathilda's impressions (Singin' in the Rain, Madonna)
Léon learning to read (the note scene)
ideas: Swap 'Cannoli' note for 'Mathilda's pick, no questions'.
Swap 'Champagne' note 'Over eighteen only' for 'Mathilda would like one. Léon says no.'
Add 'Give it roots' as the line under The Window Pot in place of 'Likes the sun'.
Swap the 'Thursday nights, a little Beethoven' footer for 'Sunday nights, a little Beethoven', a nod to Stansfield's speech.
